### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via email_domain (literal, a string literal in isAdmittedByInvitationAlone; a string literal in isAdmittedByPostureRule))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via email_domain (literal, a string literal in isAdmittedByInvitationAlone; a string literal in isAdmittedByPostureRule))_
- `content/docs/deployment/tenancy-modes.mdx`  _(via email_domain (literal, a string literal in isAdmittedByInvitationAlone; a string literal in isAdmittedByPostureRule))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via email_domain (literal, a string literal in isAdmittedByInvitationAlone; a string literal in isAdmittedByPostureRule))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via email_domain (literal, a string literal in isAdmittedByInvitationAlone; a string literal in isAdmittedByPostureRule))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via email_domain (literal, a string literal in isAdmittedByInvitationAlone; a string literal in isAdmittedByPostureRule))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via email_domain (literal, a string literal in isAdmittedByInvitationAlone; a string literal in isAdmittedByPostureRule))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e86eaa0c85cfb3f1b32a02197724de0ca5525987` — the merge of head `ffffab17796cbb730feccdd343962ce1f65aedc9` into base `8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e86eaa0c85cfb3f1b32a02197724de0ca5525987 && git checkout e86eaa0c85cfb3f1b32a02197724de0ca5525987
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d ffffab17796cbb730feccdd343962ce1f65aedc9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d && git merge --no-ff ffffab17796cbb730feccdd343962ce1f65aedc9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ffffab17796cbb730feccdd343962ce1f65aedc9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.self-registration-permission-set-reaches-invited-sign-ups.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.ts (the admission verdict and the settle classification the entry describes), and, because the PR also declares a narrowing, the pins that hold it: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-acceptance-verified-address.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/presented-invitation.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/signup-organization-census-walled.dogfood.test.ts. Read, not reviewed (outside the diff): `auth-manager-membership-admission.ts`, `auth-manager.ts` (grant staging and settle), `boot-sign-in-reachability.ts`, `packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts`. The changeset and `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` are prose faces, the lane seat's ACCEPT.

Inputs: card #34971 with all twelve comments (ruling A is 7063136215, analysis 7062693710), PR #36312 body and comments, the net diff of 8 files against merge-base `a5a5312ff4`, and the check-runs on the head. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ① Derived judgments

- Admission accept set (who may come into existence): no creation is newly admitted. `isAdmittedByPostureRule` answers true only where the old code already admitted, by the invitation branch or by the `open` / on-allowlist arm of the switch. Right.
- Admission accept set, narrowed: an invited self-serve sign-up under `open`, or on the allowlist under `email_domain`, now enters the grant path, so an unresolvable declared set refuses it `403 AUTH_CONFIG_ERROR` where the invitation admitted it ungranted. This is the narrowing ruling A accepted. Declared `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, BREAKING, `!` title. Right.
- Grant population, widened: the same two rows now receive the declared `selfRegistrationPermissionSet`. This is an authorization effect, not a relaxed accept set and not a public surface, so it does not turn the value to `yes`; it is why the PR carries `Security-touching: yes` and this tier. Right.
- Public surface: none. `isAdmittedByPostureRule` is module-private; the signatures of `decideAudienceAdmission` and `isAdmittedByInvitationAlone` and the `AudienceAdmission` type are unchanged; no error code is added.
- `isAdmittedByInvitationAlone`: rewritten onto the shared classification and behaviour-identical to main on every input (invalid, non-self-serve, `open`, `invite_only` by proof, `email_domain` on and off the list). Right.
- Published spec: one new semantic migration entry under the protocol-18 step; no schema key, accepted value or default moves. Right.
- Unchanged and pinned by controls: `invite_only` with a presented invitation (no grant), `email_domain` off the list (account, no grant, unbound until acceptance, a missing set does not refuse it), the social-provider address rule (still ahead of the posture rule), operator, provider and bootstrap creations.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and on `@objectstack/spec`. With `Metadata-protocol: none` the level is `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3). The spec bump is owed because the entry ships in the spec dist. Matches what the diff publishes.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. The analysis left this to the contract review (`none` or `semantic`). The published meaning of the key on main is "the permission set a SELF-REGISTRANT receives ... dangling declaration ⇒ nobody is admitted ungranted" (`auth-config.zod.ts`); the diff brings the runtime to that sentence for one population and changes nothing an author can write, nor the meaning or default of anything written. The semantic entry is the upgrade notice for the runtime break, not a protocol change.
- Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` is the right spelling, on the PR body and the changeset body alike. The dev's deviation note (the analysis suggested `yes (narrowing)`) is answered: the question the value answers is whether the card relaxes a published accept set or widens the public surface, and it does neither; who receives a grant is not an accept set.
- ADR-0087: exactly one marker, `registered self-registration-permission-set-reaches-invited-sign-ups`, matching the entry id; the registration gate is green on the head.
- Gate verdicts are the head's check-runs: 60 success, 10 skipped (opt-in and conditional jobs), 0 failed, including Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test Core and the type-check jobs.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, `Clause-②` spelling: answered in ②.
- Dev flag, a registered semantic entry instead of the `not-required` marker #34969 and #35200 used: accepted. An operator can act on this notice (confirm the declared set is the one invited people should hold, keep it resolvable), so an entry is the better disposition, and the claim revision 7074855577 names the path.
- Dev flag, the dogfood fixture outside the claimed surface: accepted. The battery the `!` title owes went red on a fixture ruling A makes false; the fix asserts the ruled behaviour, and the surface revision covers it.
- Dev flag, first push before `overlap-check`, and one cli vitest rerun outside the verify lock: process deviations with no effect on the tree at this head; noted for the seat.
- Dev flag, the `boot-sign-in-reachability.ts` docblock: see N1 below. Escalated to the seat as a follow-up card, not fixed here.
- `open_questions`: the final dev report carries none; the two of the first report were closed by ruling A and by the re-dispatch.
- Walled tenancy, for the seat to hold with the security label: under `group` and `isolated` an invited `open` sign-up has no membership at creation, so its declared set lands on its first membership, owned by the inviting organization (the dogfood fixture now pins exactly this). The mechanism is unchanged and already applied to a registrant who signed up first and was invited afterwards; ruling A widens who reaches it. The entry's `replacement` asks the operator to confirm the set is the access an invited person should hold beside the invited role. No finding.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; the change is a pure decision function. Nothing to report.

### ④ Design judgment

`18.self-registration-permission-set-reaches-invited-sign-ups.ts`, against ruling A, the code it cites and its first consumer (`os migrate meta` and the upgrade guide):
- `surface` names the real key path (`system.AuthConfig.audience.selfRegistrationPermissionSet`, the root the sibling entry `audience-posture-default-invite-only` uses) and the exact population.
- `reason` holds sentence by sentence against the tree: on main the invitation was read before the posture rule and answered no grant whether or not the set resolved; the settle already classified the sign-up as posture-admitted (`isAdmittedByInvitationAlone` answered false under `open` and for an on-list address); the refusal code is `AUTH_CONFIG_ERROR` with status 403 and no user row (pinned at the end of the chain for both postures and both states); the two invitation-alone admissions ask for no set.
- `replacement` is actionable and true: an administrator's creation is the `operator` class, admitted with no self-registration grant.
- `acceptanceCriteria` is a check an operator can run, and holds on `single` (grant at creation beside the default membership) and behind a wall (grant on the first membership, the one the accepted invitation writes).
- No `relevantWhen`: correct. The posture and the set can be stored at runtime through the settings console, so no top-level stack key can prove the surface absent, and the entry must always be listed.
- No tombstone and no D2 conversion: correct, no key moves.

`audience-posture.ts`, against the contract:
- Order in `decideAudienceAdmission` matches its docblock: class exemptions, bootstrap, vocabulary guard, social-provider address rule, posture rule with the grant, invitation carve-out with no grant, refusal. The posture rule sits after the social rule, so an unverified social creation holding an invitation is still refused.
- The grant path in `validateAudienceAdmission` is untouched and already refuses on `grantPermissionSet: true` with an unresolvable set, so the narrowing is reached by the verdict alone, as the PR states.
- Tried to break it: an invalid posture (refused before either reader, and `isAdmittedByPostureRule` answers false on it); an address with no domain under `email_domain` (off the list, so invitation-alone as before); a creation with no email under `open` (admitted with the grant flag as on main, nothing staged); provider and operator classes (return before the new branch); a verdict and settle that disagree (both read one function, and the only inputs where they could differ are covered by the on-list and `open` pins). None breaks.
- Module doc, the `isAdmittedByInvitationAlone` doc and the fail-posture paragraph each state the new exception and agree with the code.
- Pins: the verdict table (six rows), the four end-of-chain refusal rows, the off-list control with a missing set, the grant-beside-membership pins under `email_domain` and `open`, and the no-grant controls under `invite_only` and off the list cover every row of the PR's table. The removed `open` row of `presented-invitation.test.ts` pinned the retired branch as an instrument, as the analysis found; dropping it and keeping the off-list row is the ruled rewrite.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract; none is to be fixed in this PR outside the prose faces):
- N1 (nit): `boot-sign-in-reachability.ts`, outside the diff, says the invitation branch short-circuits before the posture switch and that the carve-out admits the one invited creation under every posture; its boot message repeats the second claim. At the verdict level both still hold (the pin in `boot-sign-in-reachability.test.ts` is green), and a configuration error was always outside that sentence (an invalid posture refuses an invited sign-up too). The mechanism sentence is now imprecise, and under `open` or on-list `email_domain` with an unresolvable set the named remedy answers `AUTH_CONFIG_ERROR`, which names its own fix. Follow-up card for the docblock and message; the seat files it.
- N2 (nit): the entry's leading comment calls this "the change of meaning the plugin-auth admission verdict landed", beside a changeset that says the key keeps its meaning. Read as the verdict's meaning it is accurate; accepted deviation.
- N3 (nit, prose face): the new `self-hosting.mdx` sentence "Under `open` every address is admitted by the posture" omits the exception the changeset states (a social creation with an unverified address while verification is in force). The page links the rule two sentences earlier for `email_domain`; a half-clause would close it, on the prose face only.
